A.explanation: Beta- decay emits a beta- particle plus an antineutrino, so the fixed decay energy is shared variably and the beta- particle shows a continuous spectrum.

B.explanation: This reverses the physics: alpha decay has no antineutrino and beta- decay does include an antineutrino.

C.explanation: The size of the alpha-particle energy does not explain why one spectrum is discrete and the other is continuous.

D.explanation: The size of the beta- particle energy does not explain the continuous sharing of energy between decay products.

hints: Notice the key contrast stated: alpha-particles from one sample all have a single discrete energy, while beta- particles from one sample have a continuous range of energies.
Think about conservation of total energy: a fixed amount of energy released in decay must be divided between all the emitted particles and the daughter nucleus.
Compare the number of particles emitted: alpha decay is a two-body split, while beta- decay has an additional emitted antineutrino that can take a variable share of the energy.
walkthrough: Identify the observation: for the same parent isotope, every alpha-particle carries the same kinetic energy, but different beta- particles carry different kinetic energies up to a maximum.
Recall alpha decay: parent nucleus goes to daughter nucleus plus alpha-particle only. With only two products, conservation of energy and momentum fixes how the disintegration energy is divided.
Recall beta- decay: a neutron changes to a proton and the emission is a beta- particle plus an antineutrino, plus the recoiling daughter nucleus.

Apply energy sharing: the total energy released is still fixed, but it is now shared among three bodies. The antineutrino can carry away a large or small fraction, leaving the remainder for the beta- particle.
This variable sharing produces a continuous range of beta- particle energies, while the two-body alpha decay gives a single discrete alpha-particle energy.
The magnitude of the energy in options C and D does not cause discrete or continuous spectra, and option B states the antineutrino is in the wrong decay. This is option A.
